Let \(a=2+\sqrt2\), so \(\frac{a}{2}=1+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\) and \(\sqrt2\cdot \frac a2=R\).

The tangency condition is
\[
\sqrt2\left|\frac a2-r\right|=R-r.
\]

Case 1: \(r\le \frac a2\). Then
\[
\sqrt2\left(\frac a2-r\right)=R-r
\]
so
\[
R-\sqrt2 r=R-r \implies r=0,
\]
invalid.

Case 2: \(r>\frac a2\). Then
\[
\sqrt2\left(r-\frac a2\right)=R-r
\]
so
\[
\sqrt2 r-R=R-r \implies r(\sqrt2+1)=2R.
\]
Since \(R=1+\sqrt2\),
\[
r=\frac{2(1+\sqrt2)}{1+\sqrt2}=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
